questions.question: In the context of ecology, what is symbiosis?

options.text: Random movement of organisms in their habitat
A close and long-term interaction between different species

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A close and long-term interaction between different species**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Symbiosis** is defined as a **close and long-term biological interaction** between two different biological species.
 
• The term originates from Greek, where "sym" means "**together**" and "biosis" means "**living**."
 
• It can be classified into different types based on the nature of the interaction:
 
 
• **Mutualism:** Both species benefit from the interaction. For example, bees pollinating flowers while collecting nectar.
 
• **Commensalism:** One species benefits while the other remains unaffected. An example is barnacles attaching to whales.
 
• **Parasitism:** One species benefits at the expense of the other. For instance, ticks feeding on the blood of mammals.
 
 
 
• Symbiosis is essential for the **balance of ecosystems**, as it allows species to adapt and survive in dynamic environments.
 
• Examples of symbiotic relationships include:
 
 
• **Mycorrhizal fungi** and plants, where fungi help plants absorb nutrients in exchange for carbohydrates.
 
• **Clownfish and sea anemones,** where clownfish get protection from predators while anemones get cleaned of debris.
 
 
 
• Symbiosis plays a critical role in **evolution, ecology, and biodiversity**, influencing species development and ecosystem interactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Random movement of organisms in their habitat**__

 __
 
• This refers to the **independent movement** of organisms without a specific pattern or direction.
 
• It is not related to symbiosis but is instead a part of behaviors like **foraging** or **dispersal**.
 
 
 
• **The process of photosynthesis**__
 __
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the process by which **plants, algae, and some bacteria** convert sunlight into chemical energy.
 
• It involves the conversion of **carbon dioxide and water into glucose**, releasing oxygen as a byproduct.
 
• While photosynthesis is a fundamental ecological process, it is not directly related to symbiosis.
 
 
 
• **Competition between organisms for resources**__
 
 
• **Competition** is an ecological interaction where organisms fight for limited resources like **food, shelter, or mates.**
 
• It can occur within a species (**intraspecific**) or between different species (**interspecific**).
 
• Unlike symbiosis, competition does not usually involve a **mutually beneficial interaction**.

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, which state from the following has the least population growth?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, Kerala recorded the **lowest population growth rate** among all Indian states.
 
• The population growth rate of Kerala stood at **4.91%**, which is significantly lower compared to other states.
 
• Kerala's low population growth rate is primarily attributed to its **high literacy rate**, better **healthcare facilities**, and widespread awareness of **family planning**.
 
• Kerala is known for its **progressive social indicators**, such as the highest literacy rate in India (around **93.91%** as per Census 2011) and one of the lowest **infant mortality rates**.
 
• The state has implemented effective **government policies** and programs that focus on improving the quality of life, which indirectly impacts population growth.
 
• Kerala also exhibits a high level of **urbanization** and better **gender equality**, which contribute to its lower population growth rate.
 
• Despite the low growth rate, Kerala is still densely populated, with a population density of **859 people per square kilometer** (Census 2011).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar**__

 __
 
• **Bihar** had the highest population growth rate in India as per the **Census 2011**, with a growth rate of **25.42%**.
 
• The high population growth in Bihar is attributed to factors such as **low literacy rates**, lack of widespread awareness about **family planning**, and socio-economic challenges.
 
• Bihar is also characterized by a **high fertility rate**, which significantly contributes to its population growth.
 
 
 
• **Haryana**__
 __
 
• **Haryana** had a population growth rate of **19.90%** as per the **Census 2011**.
 
• The state has witnessed steady population growth due to factors such as **industrialization** and increasing **urbanization**.
 
• Haryana's proximity to the National Capital Region (NCR) has also contributed to its population increase.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu**__
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu** recorded a population growth rate of **15.61%** as per the **Census 2011**.
 
• The state's population growth rate is moderate, influenced by its **high literacy rate** and progressive **healthcare initiatives**.
 
• Tamil Nadu has a higher level of **urbanization** compared to many other states, which contributes to stabilized population growth.

questions.question: Which Act, enacted in 1919, introduced the system of dyarchy in the provinces of British India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Government of India Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India Act of 1919**, also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, introduced the system of **dyarchy** in the provinces of British India.
 
• Under the system of dyarchy, the provincial subjects were divided into two categories: **“Transferred” and “Reserved” subjects**.
 
• The **“Transferred subjects”** were administered by ministers appointed from elected members of the provincial legislative councils, while the **“Reserved subjects”** were administered by the Governor and his Executive Council.
 
• This act aimed to introduce limited self-governance and prepare Indians for eventual self-rule, as per the promise made by Edwin Montagu, the Secretary of State for India, in his **August 1917 Declaration**.
 
• The act also expanded the provincial legislative councils and introduced **separate electorates** for different communities, including Muslims, Sikhs, and Anglo-Indians.
 
• This was a significant step in the gradual devolution of power from the British to Indian hands, although it was criticized for being insufficient and maintaining British dominance in key areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vernacular Press Act**__

 __
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act** was enacted in **1878** by Lord Lytton to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press.
 
• This act aimed to suppress the criticism of British policies by Indian vernacular newspapers.
 
• It allowed the government to confiscate the printing press, paper, and other materials of any publication that published anti-British content.
 
• The act was highly controversial and led to widespread opposition, eventually being repealed in **1881** by Lord Ripon.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act**__
 __
 
• The **Indian Councils Act** of **1892** increased the size of the legislative councils and allowed for the discussion of the budget.
 
• This act also introduced the concept of **indirect elections** to legislative councils.
 
• Although a step forward, it was limited in scope and did not grant significant powers to the councils.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act**__
 
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was passed in **1919** and gave the British government sweeping powers to suppress political activities.
 
• It allowed for the arrest and detention of individuals without trial and curtailed civil liberties such as freedom of expression.
 
• This act led to widespread protests, including the infamous **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**.

questions.question: Who was given the landmark contribution to the development of the second five-year plan?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**PC Mahalanobis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PC Mahalanobis** was an Indian statistician and economist known for his significant contributions to the field of statistics and economic planning in India.
 
• He is often referred to as the **‘Father of Indian Statistics’** for his pioneering work in applying statistical methods to socio-economic planning.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956–1961) focused on the development of the industrial sector in India and was based on the **Mahalanobis Model**.
 
• The **Mahalanobis Model** gave priority to the establishment of basic industries such as steel, heavy machinery, and heavy electrical equipment, which were vital for long-term economic growth.
 
• He founded the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** in 1931, which became a hub for research in statistical methods and their application in economic planning.
 
• The model emphasized the role of capital goods industries and aimed to reduce dependence on imports by promoting self-reliance through industrialization.
 
• **PC Mahalanobis** was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, India’s second-highest civilian honor, in 1968 for his contributions to economic planning and statistics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **JM Keynes**__

 __
 
• **John Maynard Keynes** was a British economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics.
 
• He is most well-known for his work in developing **Keynesian economics**, which emphasizes the role of government intervention in stabilizing the economy during recessions.
 
• His seminal work, "**The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money**", introduced concepts like aggregate demand and fiscal policy.
 
• Although his ideas influenced global economic policy, he was not directly involved in India’s Five-Year Plans.
 
 
 
• **CD Deshmukh**__
 __
 
• **Chintaman Dwarkanath Deshmukh** was the first Indian to serve as the **Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, from 1943 to 1949.
 
• He later served as India’s **Finance Minister** from 1950 to 1956, playing a key role in shaping India’s economic policies.
 
• While he contributed to India’s economic development, he was not the architect of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **JK Mehta**__
 
 
• **Jagdish Karunesh Mehta** was an Indian economist known for his work in the field of **philosophical economics**.
 
• He developed the concept of the **‘Wantlessness Curve’**, which focused on utility and human welfare.
 
• His contributions were more theoretical and were not directly related to the practical framework of the Second Five-Year Plan.

questions.question: Which two water streams meet at Tandi near Keylong in Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chandra and Bhaga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chandra** and **Bhaga** rivers originate from the **Bara-lacha La Pass** in the **Lahaul-Spiti region** of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• These rivers flow in opposite directions before meeting at **Tandi**, near **Keylong**, in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• After their confluence, they together form the **Chenab River**, which is one of the five major rivers of the **Indus River system**.
 
• The Chenab River flows through **Jammu and Kashmir** before entering Pakistan, where it ultimately joins the **Indus River**.
 
• The region where Chandra and Bhaga meet is known for its breathtaking **natural beauty** and is a significant point of interest for tourists and trekkers.
 
• The area around Tandi is located in the **Lahaul Valley**, which is known for its **rugged terrain**, **cold desert climate**, and **Buddhist monasteries**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bindusara and Sabari**__

 __
 
• **Bindusara** is a small river that flows in the **state of Maharashtra** and is a tributary of the Godavari river.
 
• **Sabari**, on the other hand, is a tributary of the **Godavari River** and flows through **Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• These rivers do not meet at Tandi or anywhere in Himachal Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Panzara and Waghur**__
 __
 
• **Panzara** and **Waghur** are rivers that flow in the **state of Maharashtra**.
 
• They are tributaries of the **Tapti River**.
 
• These rivers are located far from Himachal Pradesh and do not meet at Tandi.
 
 
 
• **Penuganga and Warda**__
 
 
• **Penuganga** and **Warda** are tributaries of the **Godavari River**.
 
• They flow through the **states of Maharashtra and Telangana**.
 
• These rivers are geographically distant from the Lahaul-Spiti region of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.question: What is the Vedic name of the river Sutlej, which is a part of the Sapta Sindhu rivers mentioned in the Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shutudri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shutudri** is the Vedic name of the modern-day **Sutlej River**.
 
• It is one of the rivers mentioned in the **Sapta Sindhu** (Seven Rivers) in the **Rigveda**.
 
• The Sutlej originates from the **Rakshastal Lake** near Mount Kailash in Tibet, which is considered sacred in both **Hinduism** and **Buddhism**.
 
• In the Vedic period, the river held significant importance for the **Indus Valley Civilization** as it was a major source of water and fertile land.
 
• The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the Punjab region and is a tributary of the **Indus River**.
 
• It is an essential part of the **Indus Water Treaty**, signed between **India and Pakistan** in 1960, which governs the distribution of water from the Indus River and its tributaries.
 
• The Sutlej is also important for the construction of several dams and hydroelectric projects, such as the **Bhakra Nangal Dam**, which is one of the largest multipurpose projects in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purushini**__

 __
 
• **Purushini** is the Vedic name of the **Ravi River**.
 
• The Ravi River is another of the **Sapta Sindhu** rivers mentioned in the **Rigveda**.
 
• It originates from the **Bara Bhangal** region of Himachal Pradesh and flows through India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Askini**__
 __
 
• **Askini** is the Vedic name of the **Chenab River**.
 
• The Chenab is also part of the **Sapta Sindhu** and originates from the **Baralacha Pass** in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The river flows through Jammu and Kashmir, India, and into Pakistan, contributing significantly to the Indus River system.
 
 
 
• **Vitasta**__
 
 
• **Vitasta** is the Vedic name of the **Jhelum River**.
 
• The Jhelum originates from a spring at **Verinag** in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It has significant historical and cultural importance, especially in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.question: Name a crystal-like, white compound with strong pungent aroma and taste, which is purified by the process of sublimation.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Camphor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Camphor** is a **white, crystalline compound** that has a **strong, pungent aroma and taste**.
 
• It is commonly obtained from the wood of the **camphor tree (Cinnamomum camphora)**, which is native to **Asia**.
 
• The compound is purified by the process of **sublimation**, where it transitions directly from a solid to a gaseous state without passing through a liquid phase.
 
• Camphor is widely used for its **medicinal properties**, such as in the treatment of **coughs, colds, and skin irritations**.
 
• It is also used in **religious rituals** and as a key ingredient in some **aromatic products**, such as incense and balms.
 
• Camphor has a cooling effect and is used in **topical applications** to relieve pain and inflammation.
 
• Its strong aroma is effective in **repelling insects**, making it a common choice for use in mothballs and insect repellents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lye**__

 __
 
• **Lye** is a strong alkaline compound, primarily composed of **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** or **potassium hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• It is commonly used in the production of **soap**, **cleaning agents**, and in **food preparation**, such as curing olives and making pretzels.
 
• Lye is highly corrosive and does not possess the **aromatic properties** or the ability to undergo sublimation like camphor.
 
 
 
• **Caustic Potash**__
 __
 
• **Caustic Potash** is another name for **potassium hydroxide (KOH)**, a strong base.
 
• It is used in **soap making, fertilizers, batteries**, and as an electrolyte in certain applications.
 
• Unlike camphor, it does not exhibit a strong aroma or undergo sublimation.
 
 
 
• **Soda Ash**__
 
 
• **Soda Ash**, also known as **sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃)**, is a water-soluble salt.
 
• It is primarily used in the production of **glass, detergents, and paper**.
 
• Soda Ash lacks the characteristic strong aroma and sublimation properties of camphor.

• The **Baiga dance** is a traditional and cultural dance form of the **Baiga tribal community**, primarily found in the central Indian states of **Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The dance is deeply rooted in the **rituals and traditions** of the Baiga tribe and is often performed during **festivals, weddings, and other celebrations**.
 
• The dance is notable for its **graceful movements** and the use of colorful traditional attire, reflecting the **rich cultural heritage** of the Baiga community.
 
• By promoting the Baiga dance, Arjun Singh Dhurve has played a significant role in **preserving the cultural identity** of the Baiga tribal group and spreading awareness about their unique traditions.
 
• The recognition of his work through the **Padma Shri** highlights the importance of safeguarding **tribal art forms** as part of India’s cultural diversity.

__
 
• **Pung Cholom dance**__

 __
 
• The **Pung Cholom** is a traditional dance form of the **Manipuri culture**, performed mainly in the northeastern state of **Manipur**.
 
• This dance combines **martial arts, acrobatics, and rhythmic drumming** using a traditional percussion instrument called the **Pung**.
 
• It is often performed during **religious festivals** and is a key element of the **Ras Leela dance-drama**.
 
 
 
• **Daph dance**__
 __
 
• The **Daph dance** is a folk dance primarily from the northern Indian state of **Haryana**.
 
• The dance is performed in accompaniment with the **Daph or Dafli instrument**, a type of tambourine.
 
• It is often showcased during **festivals and fairs** and is a part of the rich folk traditions of North India.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution requires the State to promote the economic interests of the weaker sections of society?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 46**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 46** of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It directs the State to promote the **educational and economic interests** of the weaker sections of society, particularly the **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST).**
 
• The Article ensures special attention to these communities to reduce inequalities and provide social justice.
 
• Article 46 also prohibits any form of exploitation or discrimination against these weaker sections.
 
• The DPSPs, including Article 46, are **non-justiciable** in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court. However, they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Major policies and schemes such as the **Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC/ST** and **Skill Development Programs** are inspired by Article 46.
 
• This Article aligns with the broader goals of **social equality** and **inclusive growth** as envisioned in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 47**__

 __
 
• **Article 47** of the Indian Constitution enjoins the State to raise the level of nutrition, the standard of living, and public health of its people.
 
• It also includes a directive to prohibit the consumption of **intoxicating drinks and drugs**, except for medicinal purposes.
 
 
 
• **Article 49**__
 __
 
• **Article 49** relates to the protection of **monuments, places, and objects of national importance.**
 
• The State is mandated to safeguard such sites from destruction, disfigurement, or damage.
 
 
 
• **Article 48**__
 
 
• **Article 48** directs the State to organise **agriculture and animal husbandry** on modern and scientific lines.
 
• It also advocates for the prohibition of the slaughter of **cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle.**

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are other historical names for table tennis?

a. Gossima

b. Whiff-whaff

c. Ping-pong

options.text: All of a, b and c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of a, b, and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Table Tennis**, also known as **ping-pong**, originated in the late 19th century as an indoor game.
 
• It was originally developed in **England** and was played as a parlor game by the upper class.
 
• The name **“Gossima”** was one of the earliest names for the game, used in the 1890s when it was marketed as a game with a light ball and small paddles.
 
• **“Whiff-whaff”** was another name given to table tennis, believed to have been coined due to the sound produced by the ball striking the paddles and table.
 
• The term **“Ping-pong”** became widely popular in the early 20th century and was trademarked by game manufacturers, particularly **Parker Brothers** in the United States and **J. Jaques & Son Ltd** in England.
 
• These names represent the game's evolution and its growing popularity across different regions and cultures.
 
• The modern name **“Table Tennis”** was adopted later and became the official term for the sport as it gained international recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gossima**__

 __
 
• The name **Gossima** was used in the 1890s when the game was sold with lightweight balls and paddles covered in cloth.
 
• The equipment used during the Gossima era was different from modern table tennis, and the game was less standardized.
 
 
 
• **Whiff-whaff**__
 __
 
• **Whiff-whaff** is a playful name derived from the sound of the ball hitting the paddle and table.
 
• This name was popular in the late 19th century and is associated with the informal, recreational origins of the game.
 
 
 
• **Ping-pong**__
 
 
• **Ping-pong** is the most commonly recognized alternative name for table tennis.
 
• The term was trademarked by manufacturers, including **Parker Brothers** and **J. Jaques & Son Ltd**, leading to its widespread use in marketing.
 
• Over time, “Ping-pong” has become synonymous with casual or recreational play, while “Table Tennis” is used for professional and official contexts.

questions.question: The first three digits of the Magnetic Ink Character Recognition number on your cheque specifies the _________ code in which you have the bank account.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**city**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first three digits of the **Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR)** code represent the **city** where the bank branch is located.
 
• **MICR** is a 9-digit code used to identify the location and branch of a bank, enabling smooth and secure cheque processing.
 
• The **MICR code** is printed on cheques using magnetic ink, which allows for machine readability and reduces errors in processing.
 
• The MICR code structure is as follows:
 
 
• The first three digits represent the **city** (usually the PIN code prefix).
 
• The next three digits signify the **bank**.
 
• The last three digits indicate the specific **branch**.
 
 
 
• This coding system is particularly important for **electronic clearing systems (ECS)** and facilitates faster cheque clearance.
 
• For example, a MICR code starting with **110** indicates a bank located in **Delhi**, as 110 is the city PIN code prefix.
 
• The MICR system was introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to streamline cheque processing and enhance banking efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Branch**__

 __
 
• The last three digits of the MICR code represent the **branch** of the bank.
 
• This helps in identifying the specific branch where the account is held.
 
• For instance, in a MICR code, if the last three digits are **002**, it could refer to the **Connaught Place branch** of a bank in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Bank**__
 __
 
• The middle three digits of the MICR code are used to identify the **bank**.
 
• This ensures that cheques are routed to the correct financial institution during clearance.
 
• For example, **500** may indicate a specific bank like **State Bank of India**.
 
 
 
• **Country**__
 
 
• The MICR code does not include any specific digits for identifying the **country** in its structure.
 
• It is used within India for cheque processing and is regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.

questions.question: Who among the following singers is the recipient of all the three awards Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**SP Balasubrahmanyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SP Balasubrahmanyam** was a legendary Indian playback singer, music director, and voice actor, celebrated for his extraordinary contributions to Indian music.
 
• He was the recipient of all three major civilian awards in India: **Padma Shri** (2001), **Padma Bhushan** (2011), and **Padma Vibhushan** (2021).
 
• SP Balasubrahmanyam sang over **40,000 songs** in multiple Indian languages, including Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Hindi, and Malayalam.
 
• He holds the Guinness World Record for recording the **highest number of songs by a singer.**
 
• He collaborated with various renowned music directors such as **Ilaiyaraaja, AR Rahman, MS Viswanathan**, and many others.
 
• He was also known for his contribution as a dubbing artist and worked on several films, lending his voice to prominent actors.
 
• SP Balasubrahmanyam is considered one of the greatest playback singers in Indian cinema history, leaving behind a legacy of timeless music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hariharan**__

 __
 
• **Hariharan** is a renowned Indian playback and ghazal singer, known for his melodious voice and versatility.
 
• He is a recipient of the **Padma Shri** award in 2004 for his contributions to Indian music.
 
• Hariharan has sung in various languages and is particularly famous for his collaborations with the composer **AR Rahman** in Tamil and Hindi films.
 
 
 
• **MM Keeravani**__
 __
 
• **MM Keeravani** is an acclaimed Indian music composer and playback singer, widely recognized for his work in Telugu cinema.
 
• He is known internationally for composing the music for the blockbuster film **RRR**, which won an **Academy Award** for Best Original Song ("Naatu Naatu").
 
• He has received several awards, including National Film Awards and Filmfare Awards, but does not hold the three civilian awards mentioned in the question.
 
 
 
• **AR Rahman**__
 
 
• **AR Rahman** is an Oscar-winning Indian music composer, singer, and songwriter, known for revolutionizing Indian film music.
 
• He is a recipient of the **Padma Shri** (2000) and **Padma Bhushan** (2010), but he has not received the **Padma Vibhushan** award.
 
• Rahman is globally recognized for his work on films like **Slumdog Millionaire, Roja, and Dil Se**.
